name: Scenarios
description:
Scenarios are concise narratives describing how a person or group might encounter and use a design within a particular situation. They connect users, goals, context and sequences of activity, allowing designers to consider an experience over time rather than as isolated interface elements.

Scenarios may describe existing situations or explore proposed futures.
whenToUse: Use scenarios when developing or evaluating how a concept fits into people's activities and when a sequence needs to be understood before detailed interaction design.
steps: Define the person or actor involved.
Establish a specific context and goal.
Describe the situation that triggers the interaction.
Narrate the significant actions and responses.
Include contextual constraints and interruptions where relevant.
Identify points where the design supports or obstructs the goal.
Develop alternative scenarios representing different conditions.
Use the narratives to inform requirements, flows or prototypes.
lookOutFor: Scenarios can easily become idealised stories in which everything works as the designer hopes.
Include edge conditions and interruptions rather than modelling only the happy path.

resources.citation: Carroll, J. M. (2000). *Making Use: Scenario-Based Design of Human-Computer Interactions*. MIT Press.
